family_transplant.verdict: false positive: shares no callee, field offset, or constant with the retained assembly -- only the generic register-shuffle prologue shape matched. Discarded; this draft is built from the retained assembly and its real call targets only.

notes: Reads Data_03001f2c (the polymorphic menu-runtime cell) as a view exposing a saved window handle at +44 and a 5-column-per-row u16 item-slot grid at +456, indexed by row = *(sel+8) and column = *(sel+16) from the caller-supplied selection-state pointer (arg2). This same +44/+456 view and row*5+col indexing is corroborated by menu/select_quantity.c (Func_08015270(window), Func_080030f8(1) at the same call sites) and by menu/draw_page_indicator.c's real prototype for Func_08015280(s32 window, s32 tile, s32 x, s32 y, s32 style), which matches this owner's calls exactly.

First block: if the currently selected grid cell holds an item, draws its name-ish message ((rawSlot & 0x3fff) + 0x53a, base unconfirmed -- games/gs1/assets/text/message_archive.json does not resolve id 0x53a to readable text under the simple bank*256+offset scheme), draws an icon-area rect (Func_08015068), then looks the item up via Func_08077080 and inspects byte offsets [1], [2], [12] of the returned pointer. Offsets 2 and 12 line up exactly with item.h's ItemDefinition.type (0x02) and ItemDefinition.use_type (0x0c) LAYOUT_OFFSET_GUARDs, so item.h's struct is reused (via raw u8 casts, since offset 1 -- the high byte of ItemDefinition.price -- is not a guarded field). The three literal message ids loaded at the end of the function (0xb13/0xb14/0xb15) resolve in message_archive.json to 'Can be used in Battle' / 'Can be used in Towns/Dungeons' / 'Can be used in Towns/Dungeons/Battle' -- a strong, confirmed match for the item-usability flag logic decoded from byte offsets 1 and 12 (bits 0x40 and 0x80 of offset 1, overridden to at-least-'dungeon' when offset 12 is nonzero).

Second block: loops the 5 columns of the selected row, looks each slot's item up the same way, and draws either a single 19-wide cursor rect (item type == 4) or a type icon (Func_08015280, tile = type+1) plus two cursor rects (widths 15 and 3), with field 14 on the selected column and 15 elsewhere. This is very likely the highlighted-row redraw for an equip/item selection grid (5 items per party member row), called after the cursor moves.

Every callee's argument count, order, and constant operands (call targets, the 0x3fff mask, the 0x53a add, the three message ids, all x/y/width/style constants) are confirmed instruction-by-instruction against games/gs1/asm/080a8d34.s and match the reference exactly. The residual is register-color and post-call reload-conservatism: this build's register allocator assigns fp/sl and r8/r9 to the same two long-lived values (the selection-state pointer and the dereferenced menu pointer) in the opposite pairing from the reference, and it keeps several memory-derived values (grid[cell], sel->8, sel->16) live across intervening bl calls in registers where the reference reloads them from memory after every call. Several source-level rewrites (readback ordering, mask/base as named locals, an explicit `height` local for the loop's constant arg 5, hoisting vs. duplicating the per-column item lookup across the i==selected branch, inverted-branch polarity for the kind==4 case) were tried against candidate-show --align; each changed the halfword/instruction counts but none closed the gap or found a lever that reliably narrows it further, consistent with this project's documented register-letter-swap residual class.

The family-transplant matcher's best guess (shop/select_repair_item.c, 7384/10000, below the 7500 threshold) was read and shares no callee, field offset, or constant with this owner -- confirmed false positive, discarded per the task brief.
Not adopted: differing_halfwords=223 of 262 reference halfwords, class=wrong. Retained assembly remains authoritative.

Recovered only from retained owner assembly, already-adopted exact GS1 EN sources (item.h, menu/select_quantity.c, menu/draw_page_indicator.c), games/gs1/assets/text/message_archive.json, and the approved compiler. No other decompilation project or symbol map was consulted.
